requirements.label: 128 Total Credits
requirements.hint: All College of Engineering BSE programs require 128 credit hours.

requirements.label: MATH 115: Calculus I
requirements.hint: Part of the 16 credit CoE mathematics core. AP calculus credit counts here automatically. Honors math sequences also satisfy this per the CoE Bulletin, use the adjust control if your credit posted under a different course number.

requirements.label: MATH 116: Calculus II
requirements.hint: Part of the 16 credit CoE mathematics core. AP calculus credit counts here automatically. Honors math sequences also satisfy this per the CoE Bulletin, use the adjust control if your credit posted under a different course number.

requirements.label: MATH 215: Multivariable Calculus
requirements.hint: Part of the 16 credit CoE mathematics core.

requirements.label: MATH 216: Differential Equations
requirements.hint: Part of the 16 credit CoE mathematics core. Some programs substitute a different fourth math course, see your program rows below.

requirements.label: Chemistry core
requirements.hint: Either CHEM 130 with the CHEM 125 and 126 labs, or CHEM 210 with the CHEM 211 lab for students who place into organic chemistry. Satisfactory AP chemistry credit also meets this per the CoE Bulletin, use the adjust control if that is your case.

requirements.label: CHEM 130 with labs 125 and 126
requirements.hint: General chemistry with both laboratory courses.

requirements.label: CHEM 210 and CHEM 211
requirements.hint: Organic chemistry path for students who place into CHEM 210. Placement here means no credit is given for CHEM 130.

requirements.label: PHYSICS 140: General Physics I
requirements.hint: CoE physics core. The honors sequence PHYSICS 160 also satisfies this.

requirements.label: PHYSICS 141: Elementary Lab I
requirements.hint: CoE physics core laboratory. The honors lab PHYSICS 161 also satisfies this.

requirements.label: PHYSICS 240: General Physics II
requirements.hint: CoE physics core. The honors sequence PHYSICS 260 also satisfies this.

requirements.label: PHYSICS 241: Elementary Lab II
requirements.hint: CoE physics core laboratory. The honors lab PHYSICS 261 also satisfies this.

requirements.label: ENGR 100: Introduction to Engineering
requirements.hint: A grade of C or better is required. Transfer students may substitute a course meeting the LSA first year writing requirement.

requirements.label: ENGR 101: Introduction to Computers and Programming
requirements.hint: A grade of C or better is required. ENGR 151 is an approved alternative for all CoE programs.

requirements.label: Intellectual Breadth (16 credits)
requirements.hint: 16 credits of liberal arts courses, meaning courses marked HU or SS that are not also marked BS, NS, or QR. ECON 101 and 102 count by explicit exception. Up to 4 credits of approved professional development courses from other U-M schools may also count, use the adjust control to include those.

requirements.label: Humanities minimum (3 credits)
requirements.hint: At least 3 of the 16 Intellectual Breadth credits must be humanities courses. Credit by test cannot be used for this minimum.

requirements.label: Upper level liberal arts minimum (3 credits)
requirements.hint: At least 3 of the 16 Intellectual Breadth credits must be liberal arts courses at the 300 level or higher. One course may satisfy both this and the humanities minimum.

requirements.label: General electives (11 credits)
requirements.hint: Free elective credits that bring the program to 128 total. Any U-M course counts.

requirements.label: Residency (50 credits at U-M Ann Arbor)
requirements.hint: Still building automatic checking for this rule. At least 50 credits must be U-M Ann Arbor coursework, including at least 30 credits of 300 level or higher technical courses offered by the College of Engineering in Ann Arbor.

requirements.label: EECS 200: Electrical Engineering Systems Design I
requirements.hint: EE program core. A grade of C or higher is required.

requirements.label: EECS 215: Introduction to Electronic Circuits
requirements.hint: EE program core. A grade of C or higher is required.

requirements.label: EECS 216: Introduction to Signals and Systems
requirements.hint: EE program core. A grade of C or higher is required.

requirements.label: EECS 230: Electromagnetics I
requirements.hint: EE program core. A grade of C or higher is required.

requirements.label: EECS 280: Programming and Introductory Data Structures
requirements.hint: EE program core. A grade of C or higher is required.

requirements.label: EECS 300: Electrical Engineering Systems Design II
requirements.hint: EE program core. A grade of C or higher is required.

requirements.label: EECS 301: Probabilistic Methods in Engineering
requirements.hint: EE program core. A grade of C or higher is required.

requirements.label: EECS 400: ECE Major Design Experience
requirements.hint: EE program core. A grade of C or higher is required. Taken concurrently with TCHNCLCM 496 and your MDE content course. Students who already completed EECS 496 or ENGR 499 are exempt, use the adjust control in that case.

requirements.label: TCHNCLCM 300: Technical Communication for EECS
requirements.hint: EE program core. A grade of C or higher is required.

requirements.label: TCHNCLCM 496: Advanced Technical Communication for ECE
requirements.hint: EE program core. A grade of C or higher is required. Taken concurrently with EECS 400 and your MDE content course.

requirements.label: Upper level electives in at least 2 categories
requirements.hint: At least one upper level EE elective course must come from each of at least two of the six categories: Biomedical, Circuits and Solid State, Communication Control and Signal Processing, Computers, Electromagnetics and Optics, Power. These courses count within the 19 credit upper level EE elective total.

requirements.label: Category: Biomedical
requirements.hint: One approved upper level EE elective from the Biomedical category, per the ECE program guide.

requirements.label: Category: Circuits and Solid State
requirements.hint: One approved upper level EE elective from the Circuits and Solid State category, per the ECE program guide.

requirements.label: Category: Communication, Control and Signal Processing
requirements.hint: One approved upper level EE elective from the Communication, Control and Signal Processing category, per the ECE program guide.

requirements.label: Category: Computers
requirements.hint: One approved upper level EE elective from the Computers category, per the ECE program guide.

requirements.label: Category: Electromagnetics and Optics
requirements.hint: One approved upper level EE elective from the Electromagnetics and Optics category, per the ECE program guide.

requirements.label: Category: Power
requirements.hint: One approved upper level EE elective from the Power category, per the ECE program guide.

requirements.label: MDE content course (4 credits)
requirements.hint: One 4 credit Major Design Experience content course, taken concurrently with EECS 400 and TCHNCLCM 496. EECS 470 satisfies this only if completed in Fall 2025 or earlier, and an approved senior design course from another program requires a petition, use the adjust control for either case.

requirements.label: Upper Level EE Electives (19 credits)
requirements.hint: 19 credits from the approved upper level EE elective list, chosen from at least two categories. The course used as your MDE content course cannot also count here, so the audit sets aside 4 matched credits for it.

requirements.label: Upper Level EE Electives at 400 level (7 credits)
requirements.hint: At least 7 of the 19 upper level EE elective credits must be at the 400 level or higher. The MDE content course does not count toward this minimum, so the audit sets aside 4 matched credits for it.

requirements.label: Physical Electronics and Semiconductors: EECS 311, 312, 320, 414, or 418
requirements.hint: One physical electronics and semiconductors course is required. Per the ECE program guide the same course may also count toward upper level EE electives or flexible technical electives.

requirements.label: Flexible Technical Electives (9 credits)
requirements.hint: Still building automatic checking for this rule. 9 credits of flexible technical electives are required from the ECE approved list of advanced courses in engineering, mathematics, the physical sciences, and other technically relevant fields, with at most 4 credits of independent study.
